# openmetadata_api_service (Resource)

Manages an OpenMetadata API service. An API service registers a connection to a REST or webhook source so its API collections and endpoints can be ingested.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "openmetadata_api_service" "payments" {
  name         = "payments-api"
  service_type = "Rest"
  display_name = "Payments API"
  description  = "REST API that serves payment operations."

  connection_config = jsonencode({
    type = "Rest"
    openAPISchemaConnection = {
      openAPISchemaURL = "https://petstore3.swagger.io/api/v3/openapi.json"
    }
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) API service name. Changing it replaces the service, because the name is also its fully qualified name.
- `service_type` (String) OpenMetadata API service type: Rest or WEBHOOK. The server fixes it at creation, so changing it replaces the service.

### Optional

- `connection_config` (String, Sensitive) Connector configuration as a JSON object string. Its shape depends on service_type and it may contain credentials, so it is marked sensitive.
- `description` (String) Markdown description of the API service.
- `display_name` (String) Human-readable name shown in the OpenMetadata UI.

### Read-Only

- `fully_qualified_name` (String) Fully qualified name. For an API service this equals name.
- `id` (String) Server-assigned UUID.
- `updated_at` (String) Last update time in RFC 3339 format.
- `updated_by` (String) User that performed the last update.
- `version` (Number) Server-side entity version.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by UUID.
terraform import openmetadata_api_service.payments 1f6a3a52-8d34-4f4b-9d0f-2f1c1c1c1c1c

# Or import by fully qualified name, which for an API service is its name.
terraform import openmetadata_api_service.payments payments-api
```
